# Elvis Kwame Ofori

I am a PhD Researcher and Research Assistant at the University of Galway, working across agricultural economics, land-use modelling, climate and environmental policy, and quantitative decision support.

I develop economic, spatial, behavioural and computational models to examine how agricultural, land-use and bioenergy policies move from national objectives to real production systems and places: where adjustment occurs, who and what is exposed, which alternatives are feasible, and how different policy designs may perform before major decisions are locked in.

## Current work

::: {.feature-grid}
::: {.feature-card}
### GOBLIN-Spatial
A constraint-preserving spatial foresight framework for agricultural transition incidence, response potential and land-system transformability.

[Explore project →](projects/goblin-spatial/index.qmd)
:::

::: {.feature-card}
### AGRISYN
Synthetic farm populations for representing within-area agricultural heterogeneity and supporting spatial and distributional analysis.

[Explore project →](projects/agrisyn/index.qmd)
:::

::: {.feature-card}
### IFT-BioSim
Farm-level transition bioeconomic microsimulation for heterogeneous adjustment, opportunity costs, participation and policy design.

[Explore project →](projects/ift-biosim/index.qmd)
:::

::: {.feature-card}
### BioLand-US
A U.S. implementation model linking techno-economic biomass allocation with compatible land and voluntary contractual participation.

[Explore project →](projects/bioland-us/index.qmd)
:::
:::
:::

::: {.home-section}
## Research approach

My work connects national pathway modelling with spatial reconstruction, econometrics, microsimulation, synthetic populations, optimisation, scenario analysis and reproducible research workflows. The broader aim is to build modelling and decision-support systems that can be inspected, tested, adapted and extended.

[Research themes and methods →](research/index.qmd)
:::
